doc.title: Harold Danko interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 28, 2021

title: Striker's gigs, peers, and the recommendation to Thad and Mel
summary: Playing Striker's with Konitz, he and peers formed groups, and Gregory Herbert recommended him to Thad Jones and Mel Lewis.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So it was a horrible Fender Rhodes but it was in residence there so I did a lot of gigs at Striker’s. So that was very good for me, and a lot of people do remember that club because it was pretty intimate and you know it was a chance to go hear Lee Konitz in a trio and he was pretty low profile at that point. You know I mean he was, well it was before he formed the nonet. And that was, he started getting some ideas about re- asserting himself on the scene I think, but he was not doing a whole lot other than these little gigs at Striker’s and then maybe going out and doing whatever he’d get as a solo act picking up musicians. Then from that my peers — Gregory Herbert, a great saxophonist that I became friends with with Woody Herman, we had a group that we tried to organize. So there was a bunch of my contemporaries, Jimmy Madison, a great drummer in that time, so always trying to have little gigs of our own and then it was Gregory who recommended me to Thad and Mel. And I’d known Mel from some, I think he did a week with Chet Baker that I was on. So I had this shot to play with Thad Jones and the first gig I did with them was a quartet gig, Joyous Lake I think up in Woodstock, New York, something like that.
